punchline: West's motto: not everything worth doing is worth doing well.
thirty_sec: Eagle engineers complained the goal was to "put a bag on the side of the Eclipse"; Tom West's motto was "Not everything worth doing is worth doing well", a call to spend effort on visible requirements like compatibility.
question: Which part of your current project deserves your best work, and which part only needs to function?
key_contrast: Choosing where effort goes instead of polishing every corner.
